about: Why does your unlimited data slow down? Factory #29, backlog row 33, slug unlimiteddata. One hard idea: every cell tower has a fixed amount of capacity, so when it's busy your carrier decides whose data goes first; your plan sets your place in that line, and on some plans you move back after a set amount of premium/high-speed data (T-Mobile T-Mix Saver/Standard after their 50GB premium allotment; AT&T Extra 2.0 after 100GB, Value 2.0 after 5GB; older AT&T unlimited plans after 50GB or 22GB) until the next bill cycle. The plan's FCC Broadband Facts label (required at point of sale and, per FCC 26-48, reachable from your account portal) links the carrier's network-management policy, which spells this out. Carriers' own words: 'deprioritize' is not used; they say 'may temporarily slow data speeds if the network is busy' (AT&T), 'may be temporarily slower than other traffic' / 'prioritize your data behind other traffic' (Verizon), 'reduced speeds during congestion ... due to data prioritization' (T-Mobile). Never 'throttling'. Primary sources read 2026-11-12, listed in BRIEF.md section 3. Planned silences: 0.5 s after the hook (frame-0 hit), 0.6 s after 'Until your next bill starts.' (NEXT BILL card flip), 1.2 s after 'There's the line.' (hero: re-created Broadband Facts label, coral marker circle around NETWORK MANAGEMENT, screenshot hold). Narration-led: record the voice first and key every visual beat to its word times.
